title: Contour and slice field: what does the field look like?
summary: A filled-contour map of a scalar on a plane, with a colour bar, a few contour lines and a marked slice. It is the first picture of any simulation: where the flow is fast, where it spreads and where the structure lives.

media.alt: Filled contour map of axial velocity along a jet axis, viridis colours from purple to yellow, with a colour bar and a dashed slice line at x over D equal to 5.
media.caption: Reference render with synthetic demonstration data (design-system gallery).

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: What does the field look like?
read_the_figure.axes: x: streamwise distance x/D (dimensionless, in diameters). y: transverse distance y/D. Colour: axial velocity u in m/s, from 0 to 30, on a perceptual (viridis) map.
look_at: Where is the maximum, and how fast does it decay along x?
How does the width of the coloured band grow with x?
Are the thin dark contour lines evenly spaced? Close lines mean steep gradients.
Which feature does the dashed slice line cut, and at what x/D?
read_the_figure.proves: It shows the shape and extent of a field at one instant or in the mean: its peak, spreading and symmetry. It does not give numbers accurate enough to validate; the slice profile (F10.2) does that.
if_wrong: No colour bar or no units: the colours are not values.
A rainbow map: false boundaries appear where the hue changes fast.
A grey-scale or banded map with too few levels: smooth gradients look like steps.

terms.meaning: A quantity with one value at each point, here the axial velocity u(x, y).
Regions between chosen levels filled with one colour per level.
A curve along which the field is constant. Spacing shows gradient.
A colour scale whose lightness increases steadily with value, like viridis, so equal steps look equal.
A line or plane through the field at fixed x, shown to compare profiles.

remember: Colour bar with units is the legend: no bar, no values.
Close contour lines mean a steep gradient, wide spacing a flat field.
Use a perceptual map, not a rainbow.
The slice line marks where the profile is extracted: x/D = 5 here.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Position encodes the plane (x/D, y/D). Colour encodes the value of u, using lightness that grows from dark purple to yellow. The thin dark contour lines add a second, positional cue for gradient and for reading specific levels. The dashed amber line is an annotation: it marks the location of the slice for a later profile.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: A scalar over a plane is the one case where colour is a good channel: the eye reads a map as a shape. The question is qualitative: what does it look like, where is it big, how is it symmetric. A 2D filled contour answers all of these at once, and the contour lines let the reader estimate a level and a gradient. The slice line ties the map to the quantitative profile plots.

understand.title: Read this reference render
understand.text: Q1: How strong is the field near the nozzle and how fast does it fall? The yellow core at x/D near 0 is about 30 m/s, the centreline is about 18 m/s at x/D = 5 and 13 m/s at x/D = 10. Q2: What is the value at the slice at y/D = 0 and at y/D = 0.5? About 18.5 m/s on the axis and about 9 m/s at y/D = 0.5 (a teal-blue colour), so the profile falls by half over half a diameter. Q3: Where are the gradients steepest? Where the dark contour lines are closest: just outside the core, between y/D = 0.1 and 0.3 for x/D below 2; further downstream the lines open up, the shear layer has thickened.

understand.title: The must-check list, explained
understand.text: A colour bar with units and a perceptual map are the two conditions that make the colours values instead of decoration. Both are in the figure: the bar reads axial velocity u [m/s] and the note names viridis.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: Colour is judged poorly for numbers: a difference of 2 m/s between neighbouring shades is hard to see. A rainbow map invents edges; a map with too few levels creates steps; a non-linear scale (log) without saying so distorts the gradient. A stretched aspect ratio (here x runs 10 units over the width, y runs 2) exaggerates the lateral spreading, and a single instant can hide the unsteadiness.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: Line profiles at a few stations (F10.2) when numbers matter. A vector or streamline plot for direction. Iso-surfaces (F10.5) for 3D. A difference map (model minus reference) when two fields are compared.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Add the profile at x/D = 5 as a small side panel sharing the y axis, mark the half-width contour at u = u_max/2, and set the aspect ratio to equal.

steps.title: Reading a value and a mean gradient
steps.note: Convert to a physical gradient by dividing by the diameter in metres.

steps.title: Colour resolution from the colour bar
steps.note: Differences below one level are invisible in the filled colours.

worked.title: A gradient from a contour map
worked.problem: On the slice x/D = 5 you read u = 18.5 m/s at y/D = 0 and 9.2 m/s at y/D = 0.5. The nozzle diameter is D = 20 mm. Estimate the mean velocity gradient between them.
worked.answer: About 930 per second: a shear rate of that order controls the mixing in the layer.

analyze.q: The colours near the edge look uniform purple. Does that mean the flow there is at rest?
analyze.hint: Think of the lowest colour level and what 0 to 1.7 m/s looks like.

analyze.q: What would change in your reading if y were stretched twofold?

evaluate.q: A reader prefers a rainbow map because the contrast is stronger. What do you tell them?
evaluate.hint: Which boundaries in the map are in the data?

create: Redraw with a profile panel at x/D = 5 and a half-width curve.
Draw the same field with 6 levels and with 40 levels. Which question does each answer?

checks.q: Why does the figure need a colour bar?
checks.hint: What is colour a code for?
checks.answer: Colour is a code for u; without the bar with units the colours have no values.

checks.q: The filled contour has 18 levels between 0 and 30 m/s. What is the colour step?
Contour lines at x/D = 8 are much more widely spaced than at x/D = 1. What does that say about the physics?
checks.hint: Spacing is inversely proportional to the gradient.
checks.answer: The gradients are smaller downstream: the jet has spread and its peak has decayed, so shear is weaker.
